name: Lighter chicken Caesar salad
summary: Lemon-garlic chicken sliced over crisp cos, cherry tomatoes and cucumber with oven-baked wholewheat croutons and a tangy yoghurt and Parmesan dressing.
about: Caesar salad was created in the 1920s by Caesar Cardini at his restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico, tossed at the table with a rich dressing of olive oil, lemon, garlic, Worcestershire sauce and Parmesan. This version keeps the sharp, savoury flavours but builds the dressing on yoghurt, and bakes the croutons with a single spoon of oil.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.note: finely grated, plus a little to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C if your oven is a fan oven).
Cover the chicken with cling film and flatten it with a rolling pin to an even 1.5 cm thick. Rub with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper and leave it while you make the croutons.
Toss the bread cubes with the oil on a baking tray and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp all the way through.

Meanwhile, heat a griddle or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until golden and white all the way through with clear juices. Rest it on a board for 5 minutes, then slice.

Whisk the yoghurt, Parmesan, lemon juice, garlic, mustard, Worcestershire sauce and oil together with a good grind of pepper. It should coat a spoon; thin it with a teaspoon of water if it is too thick.

Toss the lettuce, tomatoes and cucumber with half the dressing in a large bowl, top with the chicken and croutons, and drizzle over the rest of the dressing with a little extra Parmesan. Serve straight away so the croutons stay crisp.
prepNote: Bake the croutons and make the dressing a day ahead; keep the croutons in an airtight tin and the dressing in the fridge.
